rounds.proof_sketch: With feature_dim=4096, thread 255 processes idx=4088..4095 in final iteration. At idx=4095: original checks 4095<4096=true, mutant checks 4095<4095=false. Last element is skipped, causing distance calculation to miss contributions from index 4095.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation passed initial random testing because random values distribute distance contributions across all 4096 elements. The contribution from a single element (index 4095) is only 1/4096 of total distance when values are uniform, which may fall within tolerance. However, by concentrating all distance information in the last element, the mutation produces dramatically different results.
rounds.kill_strategy: Create inputs where all values are zero except at index 4095. Set anchor[:,4095]=10, positive[:,4095]=0, negative[:,4095]=10. Original computes pos_dist=100, neg_dist=0, loss=11. Mutant computes pos_dist=0, neg_dist=0, loss=1. Difference of 10 far exceeds tolerance.
rounds.recommendations: Boundary mutations in CUDA loops processing arrays should be tested with inputs that have significant values at the boundary indices (first and last elements). Standard random testing dilutes boundary contributions across many elements, potentially hiding off-by-one errors.
rounds.suggested_code:
def generate_inputs(device):
    batch_size = 128
    feature_dim = 4096
    
    # All zeros except last element
    anchor = torch.zeros(batch_size, feature_dim, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
    positive = torch.zeros(batch_size, feature_dim, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
    negative = torch.zeros(batch_size, feature_dim, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
    
    # Set last element to create large distance in pos only
    anchor[:, 4095] = 10.0
    positive[:, 4095] = 0.0   # pos_dist contribution = 100
    negative[:, 4095] = 10.0  # neg_dist contribution = 0
    
    return [anchor, positive, negative]
